sentences.text:
8 August, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.22714 Of 2015
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner seeking the following relief:
"....pleased to issue a Writ, Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the inaction of the respondent Nos.2 and 3 herein in not disposing of the representation/objections dated 26.11.2010 and consequently not depositing the compensation amount in the court as per Section 31 of the Land Acquisition Act as illegal, arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and pass such other order...."

2. The case of the petitioner company is that it is the owner and possessor of the land to an extent of Acs.2.00 guntas in Sy.No.165/2 situated at Thumkunta Village, Shamirpet Mandal, Ranga Reddy District having purchased the same from its lawful owner vide registered Sale deed document No.6647/2005, dated 30.09.2005.
It is further case of the petitioner that it made an application seeking mutation of names in the revenue records.

When the said application was rejected, the petitioner filed an appeal before the Special Grade Deputy Collector and Revenue Divisional Officer,
Ranga Reddy and the same was allowed vide proceedings No.A/3886/2008, dated 01.08.2009.

entities.text: Special Grade Deputy Collector and Revenue Divisional Officer
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: While the matter stood thus, respondent No.2 issued notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') on 13.12.2005 for acquiring the land for the purpose of Outer Ring Road.
Subsequently, an CVBR, J addendum was issued on 12.12.2008 including the land purchased by the petitioner in Sy.No.165/2.

Thereafter, Award proceedings were issued by respondent No.2 vide proceedings No.LA/Unit- IV/194/2005, dated 09.01.2009.
3.

It is further case of the petitioner that soon after coming to know about the said proceedings, the petitioner filed objections on 26.11.2010 seeking to deposit the compensation awarded for the lands in Sy.No.165/2 on the file of the concerned Court.
As the respondents have not considered the said objections and deposited the amounts as per Sections 30 and 31 of the Act, the petitioner filed the present writ petition.

4. The respondents have filed counter-affidavit stating that the land acquisition proceedings were initiated after following the due procedure as required under the Act by issuing notification under Section 4(1) of the Act and the same was published in the Gazette No.188, dated 13.12.2005.

It is further stated that after conducting enquiry under Section 5-A of the Act on 23.03.2006, only one objection petition was received and thereafter, enquiry report was submitted and draft declaration under Section 6 of the Act was given and the same was published in Gazette No.202, dated M/S. entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also stated that one K.Raja Narsaiah and others have filed claim petitions stating that they are the pattedars and absolute owners of CVBR, J the land in Sy.No.165/2 and claimed compensation under the package announced by the Government vide G.O.Rt.No.14, dated 18.12.2006.
Accordingly, the Award was passed under Section 21 of the Act through the Lok Adalat and compensation was paid to the rightful person.
The said fact was also discussed in the Award passed by the then Land Acquisition Officer in L.A./Unit- IV/194/2005, dated 09.01.2009.

It is stated that the petitioner has filed objections dated 26.11.2020 stating that he has purchased the lands in Sy.No.165/2 through registered sale deed and requested not to pay the compensation to others.

Even after knowing the publication of draft notification under Section 4(1) of the Act and draft declaration under Section 6 of the Act in the newspaper, the petitioner has not filed any objection before passing the Award, dated 09.01.2009.
Hence, the request of the petitioner was not considered.

5. Ms.Madhavi, learned Standing Counsel for the HMDA submits that since the respondents have already paid compensation to the persons, whose names are reflected in the revenue records, if the petitioner is having any grievance, the petitioner has to agitate its grievance for recovery of amounts from its vendors, who received the compensation.
CVBR, J 6.
In view of the above, it is left open to the petitioner to agitate its grievance before appropriate forum in accordance with law questioning the rejection of its objections and for compensation.
7. With the above observation, the Writ Petition is closed as no further orders are required to be passed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J Date: 08.08.2024 ssp M/S. Shantarang Estates Pvt Ltd., vs The State Of Telangana, on 8 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70572764/
